Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a soft tissue mass in the right apical region (indicated by the arrow) with associated destruction/erosion of the adjacent ribs, which is characteristic of a Pancoast tumour (superior sulcus tumour). This diagnosis aligns with the patient's history of long-term smoking and can present with neurological symptoms due to invasion of the brachial plexus or sympathetic chain.
